title: “Even to your old age and gray hairs I am He… I will carry you; I will sustain you and I will rescue you.”
paragraphs:
“Even to your old age and gray hairs I am He… I will carry you; I will sustain you and I will rescue you.”
— Isaiah 46:4
You’re afraid of becoming… too much to carry.

Too tired.
Too broken.
Too forgotten.
And the world whispers: “You’ll be left behind.”
But God interrupts that lie.
“I am He.”

Not I was.
Not I will try.
I AM.

The same God who held you when you were helpless…
The same God who carried you through sins you never talk about…
The same God who didn’t drop you when you dropped everything…

He says:
“I will carry you.”

Not when you’re strong.
Not when you deserve it.
Now. Even then. Until the end.
But here’s what we miss…
We keep trying to carry ourselves.

We drag guilt.
We hide shame.
We pretend we’re still in control.

And slowly, quietly…
we break.
Then grace steps in.

Not to shame you—
but to lift you.

Because Jesus didn’t just promise to carry you—
He proved it at the cross.

He carried your sin.
He carried your judgment.
He carried the weight that was crushing you.

And when He rose again,
He made this promise unbreakable:
You will never be too heavy for His hands.

Not your past.
Not your addiction.
Not your fear of the future.

If He carried the cross—
He can carry you.

So stop striving.
Stop pretending.
Stop running.
Let Him carry you today.
